Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

probably adverb

also most likely, in all likelihood, I suppose, I expect, presumably, likely, it is likely that, unlikely, I guess, I imagine

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.92: nōndum, opīnor, est experrēctus
Cic. Att. 9.6.2: sed, opīnor, quiēscāmus
Gell. 2.22.20: ā turbine, opīnor, ejus ac vertīgine

opīnor (ut opīnor)

verb (opīnor, opīnārī, opīnātus sum) set into the sentence, like English “I expect”

probably; I suppose, I think

Latin has no everyday adverb for “probably”: it says what the speaker supposes, with opīnor, putō or crēdō set into the clause.

Other words

  • crēdō — I suppose, I dare say; often ironic

    verb, set into the sentence · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 106: nam utī nāvī vecta es, crēdō timida es; Plaut., Ter., Cic., Caes., Sall., Liv. (Lewis & Short)

    Polite, modest or ironic (Lewis & Short): it can mean “no doubt” said with a smile.

  • vērī simile est — it is likely, probably

    with an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.5: id quod vērī simile occurrit (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 3.13.6: quod est magis vērī simile; M-O s.v. probable, likely; Traupman 340

    Cicero writes it as two words; later it is often one, vērīsimile (Lewis & Short). As an adjective, of a story or an explanation: vērī similis, likely (M-O s.v. probable, likely; Traupman 340, vērīsimilis).

  • nisi fallor — unless I’m mistaken, very likely

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.19.1: sed nisi fallor citius tē quam scrībis vidēbō; Verg. A. 5.49 (Lewis & Short)

  • probābiliter — plausibly, convincingly

    avoid · classical · Cic. Or. 122: rem breviter expōnere et probābiliter (Lewis & Short); Liv. 33.28 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short’s “probably” is the old English sense “credibly”: every classical example is of telling or arguing a thing convincingly, never “in all likelihood”.

Examples

  • nōndum, opīnor, est experrēctus

    he probably hasn’t woken up yetCic. Tusc. 1.92

  • nam utī nāvī vecta es, crēdō timida es.

    since you came by ship, you were probably frightened.Plaut. Bacch. 106

  • sed nisi fallor citius tē quam scrībis vidēbō

    but unless I’m mistaken I’ll see you sooner than you sayCic. Att. 4.19.1

  • etsī vix vērī simile est, mīsī tamen Puteolōs puerōs quī pervestīgārent

    though it was hardly likely, I still sent slaves to Puteoli to track him downCic. Att. 9.11.1

See also perhaps, I think so.
